close_reason: Updated pkix-path/README.md usage example to use TrustAnchor::from_cert(Certificate) and ValidationPolicy::new(now_unix), and validated.anchor_index.
description:
pkix-path/README.md "Usage" code block (lines 21-44) has three independent compilation errors:

1. Lines 31-35: TrustAnchor is constructed with struct literal syntax:
   ```
   TrustAnchor {
       subject: root_cert.tbs_certificate.subject.clone(),
       subject_public_key_info: root_cert.tbs_certificate.subject_public_key_info.clone(),
       name_constraints: None,
   }
   ```
   TrustAnchor is `#[non_exhaustive]` (pkix-path/src/lib.rs:418); external crates cannot use struct-literal syntax. The struct's own doc at line 415 explicitly says: 'Construct via TrustAnchor::new ... Do not use struct literal syntax.'
   Fix: `TrustAnchor::from_cert(root_cert)` or `TrustAnchor::new(subject, spki, name_constraints)`.

2. Lines 37-40: Same issue with ValidationPolicy struct literal — `#[non_exhaustive]`.
   Fix: `ValidationPolicy::new(1_780_272_000)`.

3. Line 43: `println!("trust anchor subject: {:?}", validated.trust_anchor.subject);` — ValidatedPath has no `trust_anchor` field. Its fields are `anchor_index: usize` and `depth: usize`.
   Fix: `println!("anchor index: {}", validated.anchor_index);` (and use `anchors[validated.anchor_index].subject` if the subject is needed).

Severity: P2 because this is the on-boarding example for the most security-critical crate in the workspace.

Pass-1 attribution: not addressed in commits 0d3e5db6..01908663. Add the README to a doctest target (or use `#[doc = include_str!("../README.md")]` with appropriate `# fn main(){}` framing) so the compiler enforces correctness.
title: P2: pkix-path/README.md usage example does not compile (3 errors)
